result.title: Split Federated Unlearning
result.summary: Split federated learning (SFL) combines partitioned model execution with federated aggregation to support collaborative learning across distributed Web and edge environments. However, removing learned contributions in SFL is challenging due to cross-partition coupling and historical influence propagation through dual-side aggregation. To the best of our knowledge, we provide the first systematic formulation of Split Federated Unlearning (SFU), encompassing client-wise and class-wise removal, counterfactual retraining, and partition-specific update constraints. We theoretically characterize historical influence propagation and mode-dependent unlearning feasibility, revealing structural limitations of restricted model updates. As an initial solution, we propose SURE, integrating dual-importance estimation, selective parameter perturbation, and importance-guided recovery. Extensive experiments with existing unlearning methods adapted to SFL reveal substantial forgetting-utility trade-offs across model architectures, data distributions, and update modes. SURE achieves competitive agreement with mode-matched retraining at modest additional cost, while further analyses highlight the impact of split position and update constraints on unlearning behavior. These findings establish SFU as a distinct research problem and provide a foundation for unlearning in partitioned federated systems.

AI.brief_summary: 论文首次系统形式化「拆分联邦遗忘」（SFU），刻画跨分区耦合与历史影响传播，并提出 SURE 方法（双重重要性估计、选择性参数扰动、重要性引导恢复）以实现客户端级与类别级贡献移除。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作关注分布式拆分训练中的贡献移除与隐私合规，不涉及视觉/多模态推理状态、证据获取或停止决策；其重要性估计仅用于参数级遗忘，与 LVR 的表示保留或贡献分配问题缺少可核查的具体联系。
